en: I have enclosed my resume and two reference letters.
tamil: என் ரெஸ்யூம் மற்றும் ரெண்டு பரிந்துரை கடிதங்களை இணைச்சிருக்கேன்.
context: Applying for a job by email.
explain: 'Enclosed' is formal for 'attached'. Present perfect shows the action is done now.
usage: Use it in a job application email.
leelaQ: What documents do you need for a job application?
answer: I need my resume, certificates and reference letters.

en: Would it be possible to reschedule our call to next Tuesday?
tamil: எங்க அழைப்பை அடுத்த செவ்வாய்க்கு மாத்த முடியுமா?
context: Asking to change a meeting time.
explain: 'Would it be possible to' is a polite, indirect way to ask for a change.
usage: Use it when you cannot keep an appointment time.
leelaQ: What do you say when you need to change a time?
answer: I ask if it would be possible to reschedule.

en: Thank you for your support, and I wish you all the best.
tamil: உங்க ஆதரவுக்கு நன்றி, உங்களுக்கு எல்லா நலனும் கிடைக்க வாழ்த்தறேன்.
context: Saying goodbye when leaving a job.
explain: 'I wish you all the best' is a warm, formal goodbye. It leaves a good impression.
usage: Use it in a farewell email to colleagues or a boss.
leelaQ: Whom would you thank when you leave a job?
answer: I would thank my manager and my team for their help.

en: What if we moved the launch to the first week of December?
tamil: நாம வெளியீட்டை டிசம்பர் முதல் வாரத்துக்கு மாத்தினா என்ன?
explain: 'What if' introduces a possible idea. It invites others to give opinions.
usage: Use it in a brainstorming session.
leelaQ: What idea would you suggest for your team?
answer: I would suggest a short meeting every Monday.

en: I have an idea that might save us some effort.
tamil: நமக்கு கொஞ்சம் உழைப்பை மிச்சப்படுத்தக்கூடிய ஒரு யோசனை என்கிட்ட இருக்கு.
context: Introducing an idea in a meeting.
explain: 'I have an idea' grabs attention. 'Might' shows you are not forcing it.
usage: Use it to share a suggestion with colleagues.
leelaQ: Have you ever had an idea that saved time?
answer: Yes, I used a checklist and it saved me a lot of time.

en: What do you think is the biggest risk with this approach?
tamil: இந்த அணுகுமுறையில மிகப்பெரிய ஆபத்து என்னன்னு நினைக்கிறீங்க?
context: Asking for opinions on a plan.
explain: Open questions like 'What do you think' invite detailed answers. 'Approach' means way of doing something.
usage: Use it in a planning meeting to hear everyone's view.
leelaQ: What risk do you worry about most?
answer: I worry that we may not have enough time.

en: It sounds good in theory, but I wonder how it will work in real life.
tamil: கோட்பாட்டுல நல்லா இருக்கு, ஆனா நிஜ வாழ்க்கையில எப்படி வேலை செய்யும்னு எனக்கு சந்தேகம்.
explain: 'In theory' and 'in real life' compare ideas with practice. 'I wonder' shows gentle doubt.
usage: Use it when an idea looks nice but you are unsure.
leelaQ: Is there an idea that sounds good but is hard to do?
answer: Yes, waking up at five every day is hard for me.

en: Let's brainstorm a few options before we choose one.
tamil: ஒண்ணை தேர்வு பண்றதுக்கு முன்னாடி சில வாய்ப்புகளை யோசிக்கலாம்.
explain: 'Brainstorm' means share many ideas quickly. 'Let's' invites the group to join.
usage: Use it when your team needs new ideas.
leelaQ: How does your team find new ideas?
answer: We sit together and share ideas without judging them.

en: Building on what Priya said, we could also offer a free trial.
tamil: பிரியா சொன்னதுல இருந்து, நாம இலவச சோதனையும் கொடுக்கலாம்.
explain: 'Building on' means adding to a previous idea. It shows respect for others.
usage: Use it in a meeting to connect your idea with another person's.
leelaQ: How do you respond to a good idea from a colleague?
answer: I thank them and add my own suggestion.

en: The advantage of this plan is that it costs very little.
tamil: இந்த திட்டத்தோட நன்மை என்னன்னா, இதுக்கு செலவு ரொம்ப கம்மி.
context: Explaining the benefit of an idea.
explain: 'The advantage of ... is that' is a clear way to list a benefit.
usage: Use it when you compare options in a meeting.
leelaQ: What is the advantage of your daily routine?
answer: It helps me finish all my work on time.

en: On the other hand, it could take longer than we planned.
tamil: மறுபக்கம், நாம திட்டமிட்டதை விட அதிக நேரம் எடுக்கலாம்.
context: Giving the downside of an idea.
explain: 'On the other hand' introduces a contrast. It helps you balance an argument.
usage: Use it in discussions after you mention a benefit.
leelaQ: What are the pros and cons of working from home?
answer: It saves travel time, but it can feel lonely.

en: How would this affect our current customers?
tamil: இது நம்ம தற்போதைய வாடிக்கையாளர்களை எப்படி பாதிக்கும்?
context: Asking about the impact of a decision.
explain: 'How would' asks about a possible result. 'Affect' is a verb meaning have an effect on.
usage: Use it to test an idea before a decision.
leelaQ: How would a new rule affect your work?
answer: It would change my routine and I would need time to adjust.

en: I haven't thought about that, but it's a really good question.
tamil: நான் அதை பத்தி யோசிக்கல, ஆனா அது ரொம்ப நல்ல கேள்வி.
explain: This buys you time and stays polite. 'Haven't thought about' uses present perfect.
usage: Use it when someone asks something you did not expect.
leelaQ: What do you say when you do not know the answer?
answer: I say it is a good question and promise to find out.

en: We should test the idea with a small group first.
tamil: நாம முதல்ல சின்ன குழுவோட இந்த யோசனையை சோதிச்சு பாக்கணும்.
explain: 'Should' gives advice. Testing small lowers the risk of a big mistake.
usage: Use it to advise a team before a big launch.
leelaQ: Why do people test an idea with a small group?
answer: It shows problems early before spending a lot of money.

en: Is this idea realistic given our current budget and timeline?
tamil: நம்ம தற்போதைய பட்ஜெட்டையும் காலக்கெடுவையும் வச்சு பாத்தா இந்த யோசனை நடைமுறைக்கு சாத்தியமா?
context: Questioning if a plan is practical.
explain: 'Given' means considering. 'Realistic' means possible in real life.
usage: Use it when you want to check an idea against limits.
leelaQ: What makes a plan realistic?
answer: It matches the money, time and people we have.

en: I think we are all on the same page now.
tamil: இப்போ நாம எல்லாரும் ஒரே கருத்துல இருக்கோம்னு நினைக்கிறேன்.
context: Checking agreement at the end of a discussion.
explain: 'On the same page' is an idiom meaning we all understand and agree.
usage: Use it at the end of a discussion before you move to action.
leelaQ: How do you make sure your team understands a plan?
answer: I ask everyone to repeat what they will do.

en: Don't worry, nobody will blame you for sharing a bad idea.
tamil: கவலைப்படாதீங்க, ஒரு மோசமான யோசனை சொன்னாலும் யாரும் உங்களை குறை சொல்ல மாட்டாங்க.
explain: 'Nobody' makes the sentence negative. It helps people feel safe to speak.
usage: Use it when you lead a team and want everyone to share ideas.
leelaQ: How do you help shy people speak up?
answer: I tell them every idea is welcome and ask them gently.

en: Could you walk me through your thinking on this?
tamil: இதை பத்தி நீங்க எப்படி யோசிச்சீங்கன்னு எனக்கு விளக்க முடியுமா?
explain: 'Walk me through' asks for a step-by-step explanation. It shows real interest.
usage: Use it when you want to understand a colleague's decision.
leelaQ: How do you ask someone to explain their decision?
answer: I ask them to walk me through their thinking.

en: Our priority this year should be improving customer service.
tamil: இந்த வருஷம் நம்ம முன்னுரிமை வாடிக்கையாளர் சேவையை மேம்படுத்தறதா இருக்கணும்.
context: Setting a direction in a planning meeting.
explain: 'Priority' means the most important thing. 'Should' gives a strong suggestion.
usage: Use it when you discuss goals for a team or a year.
leelaQ: What is your main priority this year?
answer: My main priority is to improve my English.

en: The more we discuss it, the clearer the solution becomes.
tamil: நாம எவ்வளவு பேசறோமோ அவ்வளவு தீர்வு தெளிவாகுது.
explain: 'The more..., the clearer...' is a pattern for two things that grow together.
usage: Use it to praise a useful team discussion.
leelaQ: When does talking help to solve a problem?
answer: Talking helps when everyone listens and shares honestly.

en: I'd rather take a little more time than make a hasty decision.
tamil: அவசர முடிவு எடுக்கறதை விட கொஞ்சம் அதிக நேரம் எடுத்துக்கறது எனக்கு பிடிக்கும்.
explain: 'I'd rather ... than ...' shows preference. 'Hasty' means done too quickly.
usage: Use it when someone pushes you to decide quickly.
leelaQ: Do you decide quickly or slowly?
answer: I prefer to think carefully before I decide.

en: Thanks for raising this; it is exactly what we needed to discuss.
tamil: இதை எழுப்பினதுக்கு நன்றி, நாம பேசவேண்டியது இதுதான்.
explain: Thanking someone for a point makes people more open. 'Raising' means bringing up a topic.
usage: Use it in a meeting when a colleague brings up an important point.
leelaQ: How do you thank someone for a useful comment?
answer: I say thanks for raising it and give my view.

en: Shall we set a clear deadline so nobody is confused later?
tamil: பின்னாடி யாருக்கும் குழப்பம் வராம இருக்க தெளிவான காலக்கெடுவை வைக்கலாமா?
explain: 'Shall we' is a polite suggestion. 'So' + clause gives the purpose.
usage: Use it near the end of a meeting to fix timelines.
leelaQ: Why do tasks need deadlines?
answer: Deadlines help us plan our time and finish the work.

en: The results have surprised everyone, including our own experts.
tamil: முடிவுகள் எல்லாரையும் ஆச்சரியப்படுத்திடுச்சு, எங்க சொந்த நிபுணர்களையும்.
explain: 'Including' adds an extra group. Present perfect shows a result that matters now.
usage: Use it when you talk about unexpected research or sales results.
leelaQ: What surprised you recently?
answer: The price of vegetables surprised me last week.

en: Let me think about it and get back to you by tomorrow evening.
tamil: நான் அதை யோசிச்சிட்டு நாளைக்கு சாயந்திரத்துக்குள்ள பதில் சொல்றேன்.
explain: 'Get back to you' means reply later. Giving a time shows you are serious.
usage: Use it when you cannot decide immediately.
leelaQ: What do you say when you need time to decide?
answer: I ask them to wait and say I will reply by tomorrow.
